The bright wall on the right checks out as the north wall, only 0.87m away at this position facing west. That confirms the pose is right, but it's odd that the gray mass isn't visible even at h=225, which sits right at the FOV's left edge — meaning the mass must be just outside the current 90° view to the south/southwest.

Actually, digging into the pixel colors at the lower-left, I notice the dark tones there (66,71,78), (35,37,41) match the chair and stool leg colors, not the gray mass. This raises the possibility that the "gray blocky mass" I flagged earlier is actually the same object as these furniture legs, sharing the same dark gray-blue palette.

I'm now reconsidering whether that gray mass could actually be the sofa. From the camera at (2.95,7.40) facing south, the sofa at (2.65,6.20) would sit almost directly ahead, roughly 1.2 meters away, and could plausibly fill much of the lower frame.

But the detected edges don't quite match a sofa surface — in f149 there's a vertical face at x=0.70 spanning y from 3.22 to 5.00, and in f150 a near boundary at x=-0.21 spanning y from 1.53 to 7.32. That 5.8-meter span at constant x seems too long to be a single object edge, which makes me suspicious of the geometry here.

Let me try computing world coordinates directly from the camera position and heading to see if that constant-x boundary actually corresponds to a point along a ray at bearing 225, checking whether the distance and lateral offset values are self-consistent.

Solving the two equations gives D+L=4.47 and L-D=-0.11, so D≈2.29 and L≈2.18, which maps to u=500 (right edge) and v≈429 — consistent with what I expected. Now I'm wondering whether this constant-x line could actually represent the base of a wall rather than just a ground boundary.

Actually it probably isn't a wall — maybe it's the top edge of a block whose top face isn't visible. Rather than keep analyzing this shot, I think the better move is to reposition: I'll translate to (2.200, 7.400) and turn to heading 225, matching f150's heading but from a new spot to get genuine parallax on the mass, since f151 at heading 270 doesn't capture it at all.

Before committing to that turn, let me verify f151's predicted pose against the known landmarks — the chair, stool, and floor lamp — by computing their expected depth and lateral offsets from camera position (2.20,7.40) at heading 270 to cross-check against what's actually visible.

Working through each: chair projects to u≈61, v≈335, matching its image position around u~30-100, base v~330-390. Stool projects to u≈86, v≈386, matching image position u~60-140, v~380. Floor lamp projects to u≈171, v≈341, matching image u~180, v~345. All three landmarks line up well, confirming this pose.

Now checking whether there's a gray mass at the left edge of the frame — I need to verify against the boundary data from the previous frame at the corresponding bearing to see if the tan floor should be unbroken there or if a mass should appear.

Actually the gray mass seems to sit south of the camera rather than along this exact bearing, since a parallel offset ray did show gray while this one doesn't. I should turn to h=225 to get direct parallax on it, since I still have plenty of frames left to spend resolving this and finishing the sweep.
